Senses.Note: The directional idiom means unconstrained movement, but Chan records keep asking who may move that way, under what permission, and whether ordinary conduct actually shows it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師一日捏拳謂眾云天下老和尚緫在這裏我若放一線道從汝七縱八橫若不放過不消一捏
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (C/C077/C077n1710.xml). Recorded Sayings of Ancient Venerable Masters. Exact utterer: Huangbo Xiyun. Huangbo Xiyun says that if he allows one line, the assembly may range freely in every direction, but if he does not, one squeeze suffices.

Occurrences.Kwic: 於一毫頭上透得。放大光明七縱八橫。於法自在自由。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2003.xml). Blue Cliff Record by Chan Master Yuanwu Foguo. Exact utterer: Yuanwu Keqin. Yuanwu Keqin says that breaking through on a single hair-tip releases great light, free movement in every direction, and freedom in the teachings.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「鍼劄不入時作麼生趣向？」師云：「我這裏七縱八橫。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB235.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lianyue. Exact utterer: Lianyue Daozheng. Lianyue Daozheng answers a question about where to turn when a needle cannot enter by saying that here one ranges freely in every direction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問如何是七縱八橫。師云。放汝一著。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1988.xml). Extensive Record of Chan Master Kuangzhen of Yunmen. Exact actor: the unnamed questioning monk. An unnamed monk asks Yunmen Wenyan about free movement in every direction; Yunmen answers that he will allow one move.

ActorAttribution.Kind: monk asking Yunmen in a public exchange
ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: the unnamed questioning monk: 問 assigns the exact headword to the unnamed monk; 師云 begins Yunmen’s answer afterward.
ActorAttribution.ReviewedBy: Codex Iriya Lane A full-case author

Occurrences.Kwic: 不到無學安能七縱八橫天回地轉哉。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T51/T51n2077.xml). Continued Record of the Transmission of the Lamp. Exact utterer: Huitang Zuxin. Huitang Zuxin says that without reaching the point of no further learning, how could he range freely and turn heaven and earth.

Occurrences.Kwic: 諸人若知去，七縱八橫，喫粥喫飯；若也不知，火爐裏東說西話
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1318.xml). Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies. Exact utterer: Cuiyan Kezhen. Cuiyan Kezhen says that those who know may range freely and eat gruel and rice, while those who do not merely chatter by the stove.

Senses.Explanation: Ranging freely in every direction describes unimpeded action rather than a literal count of seven vertical and eight horizontal paths. Huangbo Xiyun makes the freedom conditional on his allowing one line, and Yunmen Wenyan answers its direct question by allowing one move. Huitang Zuxin links the capacity to no further learning. Yuanwu Keqin explicitly glosses the resulting action as freedom, Lianyue Daozheng uses it as an answer about where to turn, and Cuiyan Kezhen joins it to the ordinary acts of eating gruel and rice while contrasting empty chatter.
